title: Non-Markovian effects on informational steady states
abstract: Informational steady states (ISSs) arise when the rate at which information is gained from continuous measurements is exactly balanced by the rate at which information from earlier measurements is lost to the environment. While ISSs have been studied in Markovian settings, relatively little is known about how memory effects influence their formation and steady-state properties. In this work, we investigate non-Markovian effects on ISSs within the framework of continuously monitored collision models. We model the environment as a sequence of two-qubit ancillas and find that, for this specific model, the steady-state information gain per measurement is negatively correlated with the degree of non-Markovianity. Numerical results further characterize how the system-ancilla and ancilla-ancilla interaction parameters influence both the degree of non-Markovianity and the steady-state information gain.
summary: This paper explores how memory effects, or non-Markovianity, alter the steady-state information flow in quantum systems undergoing continuous measurement. Using a two-qubit ancilla model, the authors demonstrate a negative correlation: higher memory effects lead to lower steady-state information gain. This provides theoretical insight into the interplay between environmental memory and information processing limits.
main_problem: The paper investigates how memory effects, quantified by non-Markovianity, influence the formation and steady-state properties of Informational Steady States (ISSs).
main_result: A negative correlation was found between the steady-state information gain per measurement ($G_\infty$) and the degree of non-Markovianity ($N_{BLP}$) for the studied model.
method: The analysis uses continuous monitoring within collision models, calculating information gain and loss rates to determine the steady state.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using continuously monitored collision models ($	ext{CM}_2$) involving a system qubit interacting with two-qubit ancillas ($Y_1$ and $Y_2$). Non-Markovianity is introduced via ancilla-ancilla interactions.
key_observables: Steady-state information gain ($G_\infty$), degree of non-Markovianity ($N_{BLP}$), Holevo Information, and the conditional state $ho_{X_t|\zeta_t}$.
important_parameters: Interaction parameters ($	heta_{XY1}, 	heta_{XY2}, 	heta_{Y1Y2}, 	heta_{Y2Y1}$), which control the degree of non-Markovianity and information flow.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes resonance ($\omega_X = \omega_Y$) and works within the framework of continuously monitored collision models.
figures_summary: Figures schematically illustrate the Markovian and non-Markovian collision models relevant to ISSs.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the ISS concept in Markovian settings, then extends the model to include non-Markovian interactions via ancilla-ancilla coupling. It calculates information gain/loss rates and quantifies the correlation between these rates and the non-Markovianity measure.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses open quantum systems dynamics by linking memory effects (non-Markovianity) to fundamental information-theoretic quantities like steady-state information flow, which is crucial for understanding measurement back-action.
